children: CBOT grain futures are lower as markets turn their focus toward meetings between the U.S. and China heading into next week. "The next big input will be the Sunday meeting between Treasury Secretary Bessent and Chinese Economy Minister He," says Charlie Sernatinger of Marex in a note. "Then the big enchilada is the Thursday meeting between Xi and Trump." The grain markets hope for clarity on forward Chinese export demand, but futures are bogged down after Wednesday's interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. Most-active corn is down 0.8%, while soybeans fall 0.3% and wheat is off 1%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
